name: Sphagneticola trilobata
description: A fast-spreading groundcover with yellow daisies that smothers gardens and bushland, especially along creeks in Queensland and New South Wales.

compost.note: Every piece of stem can take root. Please bag it rather than composting.

care_note: Please remove it completely, including every runner, and check the area again every few weeks.

name: Asparagus aethiopicus
description: A spiny, fern-like plant with tuberous roots and red berries that birds spread into bushland.

compost.note: The tubers regrow. Please bag the crowns and tubers.

toxic.note: The berries are poisonous, and the sap can irritate skin.

care_note: One of the asparagus weeds, which are Weeds of National Significance. Please dig out the central crown rather than pulling the stems.

name: Senecio madagascariensis
description: A small daisy with many yellow flowers that invades pasture and lawns. It is poisonous to livestock.

compost.note: Please bag plants, especially once they have flowered.

toxic.note: It contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which damage the liver of horses, cattle and other animals.

care_note: A Weed of National Significance. Please pull plants before they flower, wearing gloves.

name: Ochna serrulata
description: A shrub with yellow flowers and black seeds on red receptacles that birds spread into bushland. Its deep roots make it hard to remove.
care_note: An environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales. Please dig out the whole crooked taproot.

name: Schinus terebinthifolius
description: A spreading tree with glossy leaves and clusters of red berries that birds spread. It forms thickets along creeks.

toxic.note: The sap and berries irritate skin and can cause breathing problems in sensitive people.

care_note: An environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales.

name: Cinnamomum camphora
description: A large, dense evergreen tree that smells of camphor. Birds spread its black berries, and it has taken over large areas of northern New South Wales and south-east Queensland.
care_note: A major environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales. Large trees need an arborist.

name: Ligustrum lucidum
description: A fast-growing evergreen tree with sprays of white flowers and black berries that birds spread. Its pollen worsens hay fever.

toxic.note: The berries are poisonous if eaten.

care_note: An environmental weed in Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria.

name: Celtis sinensis
description: A deciduous tree whose orange berries birds spread into creeks and bushland.
care_note: An environmental weed in south-east Queensland and northern New South Wales.

name: Solanum mauritianum
description: A fast-growing large shrub with velvety leaves, purple flowers and yellow berries that birds spread.

toxic.note: All parts are poisonous, and the hairs on the leaves irritate the skin, eyes and lungs.

care_note: An environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales. Please wear gloves and a dust mask when removing it.

name: Cardiospermum grandiflorum
description: A climbing vine with inflated, balloon-like seed pods that smothers trees along creeks.
care_note: An environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales. Please remove it before the pods ripen.

name: Ipomoea indica
description: A twining vine with large blue-purple trumpet flowers that smothers shrubs and trees.

compost.note: Stem pieces take root. Please bag it.

care_note: An environmental weed in eastern Australia.

name: Tradescantia fluminensis
description: A succulent creeping groundcover that forms dense mats in moist shade and grows back from tiny stem pieces.

compost.note: Every stem piece can take root. Please bag it.

toxic.note: Contact commonly gives dogs itchy skin rashes.

care_note: An environmental weed in eastern Australia. Please rake up and bag every piece.

name: Bryophyllum delagoense
description: A succulent with mottled, tube-like leaves that grow tiny plantlets at their tips, so it spreads very quickly.

compost.note: Plantlets keep growing in compost. Please bag it and put it in the general waste bin.

toxic.note: It contains cardiac glycosides that can kill livestock and pets.

care_note: A declared weed in Queensland and New South Wales.

name: Oxalis corniculata
description: A small creeping weed with clover-like leaves and tiny yellow flowers. Its seed pods flick seeds far and wide.
care_note: Please hand-weed it before it flowers, and mulch bare soil to stop seedlings.

name: Cyperus rotundus
description: A sedge with glossy leaves and purple-brown flower heads that spreads by chains of underground nuts.

compost.note: The nuts survive composting. Please bag them.

care_note: Pulling the plants leaves the nuts behind. Please dig out the nuts, or smother the area for a season.

name: Bidens pilosa
description: A common weed with small white-and-yellow daisies that bees visit, and barbed seeds that stick to clothes and pets.
care_note: Please pull plants before they set seed.

name: Taraxacum officinale
description: A common lawn weed whose yellow flowers are an important early food for bees.

name: Trifolium repens
description: A creeping clover with white flower heads that honey bees love. It feeds the caterpillars of small blue butterflies and adds nitrogen to lawns.
care_note: Bees on clover flowers can sting bare feet. Mowing before children play on the lawn helps.

name: Soliva sessilis
description: A low lawn weed with fine leaves whose spiny seeds hurt bare feet in spring.
care_note: Please treat or dig it out in winter, before the spiny seeds form.

name: Plantago lanceolata
description: A weed of lawns and pasture with a rosette of ribbed leaves and short, dark flower spikes on long stems.

name: Euphorbia peplus
description: A small, upright weed of garden beds with milky sap.
care_note: Please wear gloves when pulling it, and keep the sap away from your eyes.

name: Sonchus oleraceus
description: A common weed with soft, toothed leaves, milky sap and yellow dandelion-like flowers.

name: Erigeron bonariensis
description: A greyish, hairy weed of disturbed ground that produces huge numbers of wind-blown seeds.
care_note: Please pull it before it flowers.

name: Cenchrus clandestinus
description: A vigorous lawn grass that spreads by thick runners above and below ground.
care_note: It invades garden beds and bushland. Please keep a hard edge between the lawn and garden beds.

name: Cynodon dactylon
description: A fine, hard-wearing lawn grass that goes dormant and brown in cold winters.
care_note: It creeps into garden beds by runners. A hard edge helps.

name: Stenotaphrum secundatum
description: A broad-leaved lawn grass that copes with more shade than couch or kikuyu.

name: Zoysia japonica
description: A dense, slow-growing lawn grass that needs little mowing.
